Moving to public safety, the precinct has been short-staffed on evening dispatch for the third month running.
Residents want a faster response time, and that means putting more officers back on beat patrol.
The warrant backlog at the precinct is also worth a closer look before next quarter's report.
Before I move on, let me note the depot expansion still needs a dedicated funding line.
Finally, the watershed assessment shows runoff from the new lots is stressing the creek's fragile habitat.
We should expand tree canopy along that corridor to cut particulate levels near the schoolyard.
Protecting the wetland buffer now will save the city far more in flood costs later.
With that, I'll close by urging staff to fold habitat protection into every future permit review.
